package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via email, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: FTCode is a malicious PowerShell-based ransomware distributed via spam campaigns. It is delivered through malicious Word documents containing macros that execute PowerShell commands to download and run ransomware, encrypting user files and demanding payment for decryption.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user opens malicious Word document and enables macros)
execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro in Word document (e.g., invoice.docm)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objShell As Object
  Set objShell = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  objShell.Run "powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command [malicious PowerShell command]"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (macro execution), the code launches a hidden PowerShell process that downloads and executes further malicious code, leading to ransomware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that launch PowerShell with bypassed execution policy and hidden windows are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal macros should not invoke PowerShell or download and execute code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation may use macros to launch scripts, but never to download and execute untrusted code.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell command downloads and executes a remote script, which is the FTCode ransomware payload, leading to file encryption and ransom demand.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote scripts is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PowerShell usage should not fetch and execute code from untrusted remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use similar commands for internal automation, but never from untrusted domains.

attack_chain.action: User receives a spam email with a malicious Word document attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens the document and enables macros.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro executes, launching a hidden PowerShell process.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell downloads and executes ransomware payload.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell downloads and executes the FTCode ransomware script from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware encrypts files and displays ransom note.

behavioral_signatures: Word documents with macros that launch PowerShell
PowerShell processes with ExecutionPolicy Bypass and NoProfile
PowerShell downloading and executing code from external domains
file_indicators: Presence of FTCode-related PowerShell scripts on disk
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to suspicious or known malicious domains (e.g., domains hosting ftcode.ps1)
Unusual PowerShell user-agent strings in network logs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that contain macros invoking PowerShell, especially with ExecutionPolicy Bypass and NoProfile flags. Detect PowerShell processes that download and execute scripts from external sources. Flag outbound HTTP requests to known FTCode infrastructure or suspicious domains. Use endpoint protection to block or alert on suspicious macro and PowerShell activity.
